title: Hosted edge retry-coalescing and graceful-fallback to prevent 5xx cascades
creator: Lina Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers escalated persistent 5xx/timeouts during mid-sized tenant bursts. Investigation revealed a cross-mode routing interaction (Hosted frontdoor -> Dedicated pools) plus misaligned retry timers producing retry storms that saturated worker accept queues and triggered transient 5xx responses. Edge kept re-routing requests during partial TLS/handshake stalls which amplified load. Impact: visible customer errors and elevated P99 latency for 3 tenants; several support tickets and an on-call bridge. Root cause hypotheses validated in staging: (1) frontend retry policy was too aggressive for long-tail handshake stalls, (2) dedicated-side admission control allowed bursts that caused KV cache eviction and worker overload without early shedding, (3) request deduplication at the gateway is ineffective for large multipart uploads because of truncated idempotency token generation. Goals: stop the immediate amplification, preserve SLOs, add dedup/coalescing to edge, improve observability and SDK guidance, and update runbooks for cross-mode escalations.
repro_steps: 1) Simulate a tenant burst: 300 concurrent requests with a 20% chance of simulated handshake stall between frontdoor and dedicated pool.
2) Use long payloads (~5MB multipart) to trigger truncated idempotency tokens on client SDK v2.4.
3) Observe edge retry attempts, worker accept queue length, KV cache churn, and resulting 502/504 surge.
4) Capture traces (frontdoor -> dedicated) to correlate retry timings and queue spikes.
impact_summary: High customer-visible 5xx rate and P99 latency degradation for affected tenants over a 45-minute window. Support tickets from 3 customers with production outages; SRE pager triggered once. Financial/SL implications: potential SLA credits if not remediated in the release window.
short_term_mitigation: Deployed edge-side soft throttle for client retries (backoff extension + request-coalescing window) to canary region at 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC. Reduced immediate 5xx amplification by ~70% for canary traffic. Also applied per-tenant temporary admission cap for the top 5 noisy tenants.
long_term_plan: 1) Implement deterministic request fingerprinting at edge (sha256 over canonicalized headers+body prefix) to dedupe retries within a 5s window. 2) Add retry-coalescing in frontdoor: hold identical requests for up to 100ms and forward one to upstream. 3) Harmonize retry timers between SDKs and edge; publish SDK guidance and add server-side idempotency acceptance for canonical fingerprints. 4) Harden dedicated admission control to early-shed low-priority requests and expose per-pool backlog metrics. 5) Add an escalations runbook entry for cross-mode routing problems with specific diagnostic traces to collect.
work_items: UPSTR-allowlist: accept deterministic fingerprints in dedicated routing (PR #12372)
SDK-PR: standardize idempotency token generation in JS/Python SDKs (PR #12401)
OBS: new metrics - edge.dedupe.rate, pool.backlog.accept_queue, retry.amplification.factor

postmortem_actions: Add automatic detection rule for retry amplification (>2x baseline) that alerts SRE and triggers a temporary retry rate limit
Ship SDK patch to canonicalize idempotency tokens and document recommended retry semantics
Expose pool-level accept queue metrics and add an early-shed policy for overloaded pools
Publish a cross-mode escalation runbook with trace examples and diagnostic queries
current_blockers: Need SDK maintainers to approve idempotency token change (blocking dedupe rollout across all regions). Coordinating security review for canonicalization rules to ensure no PII leakage.
